_comment: Planned series. `run.py series <slug>` writes the next unwritten part (or all with --all). hue/style pin the cover identity so parts look like a set. Each part: term (post subject), key (URL), brief (what THIS part must cover and must leave to other parts), seeds (source URLs).

parts.brief: Part 1: what prompt engineering still is in late 2026 now that models follow instructions well. What moved into context engineering / harnesses and what stayed in the prompt. Anthropic's and OpenAI's current prompting guides as primary sources. End with the 5 things that still move the needle.

Part 2: system prompts in production. Structure (role, rules, examples, output contract), ordering, XML tags vs markdown, few-shot vs zero-shot, how long is too long, prompt caching economics. Must include a real transcript visual: run a short prompt with and without a system prompt. Draw on our own pipeline's merger/writer system prompts as first-hand examples.

Part 3: how you know a prompt change helped. Golden sets, LLM-as-judge, pairwise comparison, regression on real traffic, the 2026-08-07 JSON-preamble incident in our pipeline as the war story (a prompt tweak that silently emptied briefings; fixed by a parser, not a prompt). Promptfoo / Braintrust / Anthropic eval cookbook as sources.

Part 1: running Claude Code headless (claude -p) as a pipeline step instead of a chat. Our daily pipeline (~10 agents) does exactly this. Cover: subscription vs API economics, --output-format json, retries on transient errors, JSON repair, the hook that blocked a run, timeouts and caffeinate. Numbered STEP sections. Include a real transcript visual.

Part 2: the failure modes that don't throw. A model that returns rc=0 with an empty briefing, a usage-policy refusal that looks like success, a hook block reported as a completed turn, stale shadow directories. Our QA evaluator + per-agent floors as the fix. What to assert after every LLM call.

OpenAI Codex (the agentic coding product: CLI + cloud agent + IDE) as it stands in late 2026. What it does well, pricing/limits, how it compares to Claude Code day to day, where it fits for an Israeli team. Must include at least one real screenshot visual of the official docs/product page and a compare card vs Claude Code.

xAI's Grok agent/bot product (the standalone agent people call 'Grok bot', and Grok on X). What it actually is, what it can do unattended, pricing, what's hype, how Israeli engineers are using it. Include a real screenshot visual. Be concrete about availability and limits; if sources disagree, say so.

The advanced ChatGPT features engineers under-use: projects, custom instructions and memory, canvas, deep research, agent mode/operator, connectors/MCP apps, scheduled tasks, plugins announced at DevDay 2026. FAQ format: real questions an engineer asks, answered with specifics and limits.

Anthropic's Claude Design (design canvas / artifacts for websites, screens, decks). What it is, who it is for, how it relates to Claude artifacts and Claude Code, what it produces, limits. Include a real screenshot of the official page. First-hand: we used it this week while redesigning this very blog and chose to code directly instead — say why, honestly.
